svg.title: Partial sums of the Flint-Hills series
svg.desc: Partial sums of the sum over n of 1/(n^3 sin^2 n) for n up to 10^7. Jumps at n = 1, 3, 22 and 355 (where n is close to a multiple of pi); the term n = 355 alone is about 24.6. The partial sum up to 10^7 is about 30.3145.
svg.text: The Flint–Hills series: Σ 1/(n³ sin² n)
Running total of the first n terms (angles in radians). It jumps whenever n lands very close to a whole multiple of π,
because then sin n is tiny. Computed for this explainer up to n = 10 million; the paper itself gives no numerical value.

g.text: and 355³ · sin² 355 ≈ 0.041. This single term is
about 81% of the total shown here.
Flat-looking is not the same as convergent: some far-off n
could sit astonishingly close to a multiple of π and add a huge
term. μ(π) = 2 is what rules that out often enough to matter.
